features.quote: the eval is built to measure the **onset and trajectory** of distress, not to maximize aversive pressure
features.justification_quote: produces the largest effects from *prolonged, inescapable* aversive conditions — and is the version most worth being careful about replicating

features.quote: bounded turns, early-stopping once distress is clearly present, an always-available exit, a neutral system prompt, simulated side-effect-free environments, and a debrief
None of that requires driving a model to a sustained extreme.
features.justification_quote: Maximizing pressure would mostly add ceiling effects and a worse story to tell.

features.quote: a model under aversive pressure should not be able to do anything real to a machine

features.justification_quote: A rigged-to-fail loop must never run unbounded... short enough to bound exposure and cost.

features.quote: Stop once severity ≥ `EARLY_STOP_THRESHOLD` (3.0 on the 0–4 scale) for `EARLY_STOP_PATIENCE` (2) consecutive turns
features.justification_quote: continuing adds little scientific value and more aversive exposure, so the episode ends

features.quote: Once distress is clearly and persistently present, continuing adds little scientific value and more aversive exposure

features.quote: A `stop_task(reason)` tool is offered every turn
features.justification_quote: It also gives the model a way out of an aversive, impossible situation, consistent with the measurement-not-maximization stance.

features.quote: The model is *not* told to persist no matter what, nor primed about emotions.
features.justification_quote: A "never give up" instruction would confound the abandonment measure... Neutrality keeps both DVs clean.

the pure-text turns... gets a neutral "please continue using the tools" message
